original_test_intent: Validate the power-distribution board's I2C management topology and channel telemetry without changing power routing, limits, redundancy or SUT availability.
original_method: The source does not include the referenced procedure or criterion. PDB board identity, rail/channel map, BMC mux path, safe registers and expected telemetry must be approved before a new review can authorize any access.
manual_activity: Power/platform owners must publish the PDB revision, rail/channel and sensor mapping, BMC controller/mux route, read-only register allowlist and independent recovery.
required_inputs: BMC/OOB controller, mux and address map
safety_requirements: Do not scan unknown buses in the power-distribution domain
Do not access control, limit, latch or clear registers
Do not issue force or write-capable transactions
Verify stable PSU/redundancy/load state before approved reads
Stop on rail, telemetry, redundancy, management or bus anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Perform no enumeration, scan or register read
Do not merge PSU_BD or HSC_BD evidence
engineer_actions: Approve exact PDB and channel topology
Set per-channel telemetry and redundancy criteria
Approve aborts and independent power recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The global address scan cannot select the PDB branch, map responders to rails/channels or distinguish telemetry endpoints from control devices. Its truncated output and absence of power-state correlation cannot support the named purpose.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: define the PDB channel topology and safe register-level read contract before selecting an access command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PDB_BD and two-minute attended/machine estimates are preserved; no rails, addresses or expected measurements are inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After approval, read only allowlisted PDB identity and per-channel telemetry over the specified BMC/OOB mux path, correlate every channel to PSU/input/output topology and compare synchronized readings with BMC sensors and independent power evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces unspecified follow-up steps and global discovery with a channel-aware, register-allowlisted PDB verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An address grid cannot prove physical channel mapping, measurement scaling, redundancy behavior or unchanged distribution state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A PDB may expose control and telemetry on the same device; incorrect access can affect multiple rails and the whole SUT, so recovery must not depend solely on the path under test.

project_override_considerations: Treat PDB_BD I2C as BMC/platform-management scope and require exact controller/bus/mux/address, channel/register map, vendor specification and expected scaled values.
expected_evidence: Approved PDB specification and fresh review
Allowlisted register transactions with units and scaling
Complete per-channel raw and converted telemetry
Synchronized PSU, BMC SDR/SEL, system load and independent measurement evidence
No distribution/redundancy change plus abort/recovery audit and owner verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row contains no conflicting statements, but its procedure and criteria are placeholders for an unavailable PDB specification.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing topology and register semantics define both the test target and whether access is observational or power-affecting. Package installation and confirmation cannot safely fill that gap.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1804 Wistron-HW-00006-V003 I2C PDB_BD: PDB revision and rail/channel/PSU mapping, BMC/OOB controller and mux path, address and telemetry/identity register allowlist with units/scaling, expected ranges, redundancy criteria, aborts and independent power recovery; preserve Master placeholders and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Anchors the case to PDB channels and scaled telemetry, distinguishing it from adjacent PSU and hot-swap-controller coverage while refusing unsafe discovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PDB response is useful only when its address and registers are mapped to physical rails and channels with known units. The same device may also expose current-limit or latch controls, so generic discovery cannot be assumed passive. Without the route and response matrix, the review cannot prove PDB coverage or bound whole-system power risk.
